newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Police arrest former cabinet minister Sirisena Cooray under emergency regulations. Cooray, a powerful politician in assassinated President Ranasinghe Premadasa's government, was planning a mass rally later this month to commemorate the late leader's birthday.
A bomb placed on a bicycle explodes in northern Vavuniya town wounding 26 people, including four policemen.
Government says more than 2,600 tonnes of food sent to rebel-controlled northern areas in 10 days to June 9 and refutes claims by Tamil Tiger rebels that food supplies have been stopped.
Police hold arrested United National Party (UNP) politician Sirisena Cooray at a government house in Colombo.
Transport ministry makes arrangements to remove some 3,888 employees of the government-owned Central Transport Board who are drawing their salaries without reporting to work.
Arrested UNP politician Sirisena Cooray says police have not informed him of any wrong-doing several hours after arresting him.
Troops kill at least 25 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels during an attack on a rebel camp in eastern Batticaloa district
